prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world each placement lands at the left-right mirror of the chosen anchor: a brick dx cells wide chosen at column x lands at column 8 - dx - x, in the same row. The valid-action mask is in the agent's own action terms. The designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
The only trial is the starting architecture. It scored 0.000 on both seeds and always ends with DONE before any placement. The untrained trace shows the reason: the action's column index is mirrored relative to the observation. A brick at action column x with width dx fills observed columns X-dx-x to X-1-x. Rows and layers are as described. The convolutional head is translation-equivariant, so it scores the wrong cells. Nearly every placement is then penalised and DONE (reward 0) takes over. The most likely fix is to re-index the head's per-type score maps so they match action coordinates. This uses only learned features, the same way the starting architecture already assumes a layout. This round tests: (1) that alignment alone; (2) alignment plus a recipe with fewer PPO epochs, which buys more samples, and more entropy; (3) a learned gate between the mirrored and the unmirrored layout, which should also work in worlds where the layout differs.

### Round 2
The action column index is mirrored relative to the observation. Remapping the head so its scores line up with the actions turned 0.000 into 0.746. Running fewer PPO epochs (2 instead of 4, which buys about 1.86x more samples), plus ent_coef 0.02, raised that to 0.877, with both seeds within 3 points. That points to sample limits, not an epoch-2 quirk, but it is one trial. A learned gate that blends mirrored and unmirrored scores failed (0.148). Dev IoU is about 0.98 while exact success is about 0.88, so most failures are small order or height mistakes. Trace 2 shows column (1,2) overbuilt to height 3 after the agent lost track of the landing layer. The next steps are: push samples further with 1 epoch; give more credit to the exact-build bonus; and add a head that can compare the landing layer with each cell under a brick.

### Round 3
Aligning the action columns with the mirrored observation was the key fix, raising dev success from 0 to 0.75. Cutting PPO epochs from 4 to 2 lifted it to 0.877 (r1c2), and r1c2's learning curve was still rising at the end, so this setup looks short of samples. Going to 1 epoch failed badly (0.20, seeds 0.08 and 0.31): the agent learned to stop early, which suggests too little optimisation per sample. Two other changes made no difference beyond seed noise: gamma 0.99 (0.870) and the two-stage head (0.833, seeds 0.79 and 0.87). Remaining errors are single wrong placements, about 0.6 extra cells per episode, often a brick landing one layer too high. Because the budget is fixed, the best options are to learn more from each sample (more gradient steps per batch, a higher learning rate) and to give the head cheap, precise per-column information. Each candidate makes one change to r1c2.

### Round 4
The big gain came from fixing the mirrored action layout. Cutting PPO epochs from 4 to 2, so the same budget buys more samples, added about 13 points. One epoch failed: the policy was under-fitted and one seed came out at 0.08. Within the 2-epoch recipe, both stronger optimisation changes helped by about 5 points over 0.877. Doubling the minibatches scored 0.933 with very consistent seeds; lr 0.002 scored 0.929. Learning curves were still rising at the end, so learning speed per sample is the bottleneck. The architecture changes either cost samples (two-stage head) or were unstable (stem skip: 0.92 and 0.32). Adding layers would cut samples, so this last round puts the trials into faster learning on the best network. Two candidates combine 64 minibatches with a larger lr (moderate and bold). The third keeps 64-sample minibatches but halves n_envs, which gives fresher rollouts and twice as many updates.

## Trial it ended with
name: r3c1 + lr 0.0015
hypothesis: Combine the two improvements, 64 minibatches and a larger lr, at a moderate lr of 0.0015. Each sample then moves the policy further while the curve is still rising, so success should go above 0.933. A full lr of 0.002 on top of twice as many steps may be unstable, hence this middle value. Refuted if the mean is below 0.92 or one seed collapses.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).
